title: A Planning Guide for Making Temporary Events Accessible to People with Disabilities
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 2015; based on the 2010 ADA Standards. Site selection decides most accessibility; accessible routes at least 36 inches wide; ramps no steeper than 1:12; at least 5% of tables accessible; assistive listening receivers provided free; advertise access; train staff.

title: ADA Requirements: Effective Communication
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Issued January 2014, updated 28 February 2020. Title III businesses must communicate effectively with people with vision, hearing or speech disabilities; auxiliary aids include interpreters, real-time captioning, large print, Braille and assistive listening devices; cannot require a person to bring their own interpreter; undue burden exception still requires another effective aid.

title: ADA Requirements: Service Animals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Issued July 2011, updated 28 February 2020. Service animals are dogs trained to do work for a person's disability; staff may ask only two questions; no documentation or demonstration; emotional support animals are not service animals under the ADA; exclusion only if out of control or not housebroken.

title: ADA Requirements: Ticket Sales
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Issued July 2011, updated 28 February 2020. Accessible seats sold in the same way, hours and stages as other seats, at no higher price in the same section; up to three companion seats; no proof of disability; rules on releasing unsold accessible seats and on the secondary market.

title: Using a range of communication channels to reach disabled people
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated 17 June 2026. Mention access facilities in publicity; check the venue; contact options beyond a phone number; ask about adjustments on forms; book BSL and other language support early; send papers about two weeks ahead; sessions of around 45 minutes with breaks; easy read booking forms.

title: Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025: statutory guidance
supports: Opened with WebFetch (first part of a long page read). Added 21 April 2026, corrected August 2026. Qualifying events: public access, entry checks, 800 or more people at once; standard tier premises 200 to 799; Security Industry Authority regulates; Royal Assent 3 April 2025 and an implementation period of at least 24 months; the person in control of the venue for the event is responsible and duties can't be handed off.

title: Temporary events notice
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. England and Wales: fewer than 500 people including staff; up to 168 hours; at least 10 clear working days' notice, or 5 to 9 for late notices; limits per person and up to 15 per premises a year (21 days total); apply to the local council.

title: Organising a voluntary event: a 'can do' guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated 25 February 2019. For voluntary and community events: think through realistic risks; public liability insurance is not a legal requirement but may be asked for; most councils need 4 to 6 weeks' notice to close a quiet street, busy roads several months; food hygiene and allergen questions.

title: Event safety: Are you a...? (roles and responsibilities)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated 16 March 2023. The event organiser has prime responsibility for the health and safety of workers, the audience and contractors; venue owners keep premises safe; shared control needs clearly assigned responsibilities and shared safety information; contractors show competence.

title: Allergen guidance for food businesses
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Publication updated 17 July 2026. The 14 allergens; allergen information for non-prepacked food in writing or verbally with a visible sign; buffets need information for each dish; written information plus a conversation recommended.

title: Food Allergies
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Content current as of 11 March 2026. Nine major food allergens: milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans and sesame (sesame from 1 January 2023 under the FASTER Act).

title: European accessibility act
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. Directive (EU) 2019/882; products and services covered include ticketing and check-in machines and e-commerce.

title: Legal grounds for processing data
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. Legal grounds including consent and legitimate interests; health and other sensitive data are special categories processed only under specific conditions; unnecessary data can't be a condition of a service.

title: Principles of the GDPR
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. Purpose limitation, data minimisation (adequate, relevant, necessary), storage limitation (shortest time, set erasure or review limits) and accuracy, with examples.

title: Can data received from a third party be used for marketing?
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. The supplier of a list must show lawful collection and permission for advertising; consent must have covered passing data on; tell people at first contact; exclude objectors; ePrivacy rules for email.

title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
supports: Opened with WebFetch. August 2023, edited January 2024. No exception for B2B email; postal address; clear opt-out honoured within 10 business days; seller and sender can both be liable.

title: Marketing and advertising: the law - Direct marketing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. Marketing emails and texts to individual customers need permission; every message must offer an easy opt-out; get permission before sharing customer details with another organisation.

title: Canada's anti-spam legislation, consolidated Act E-1.6 (sections 10 to 11)
publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Implied consent where a person disclosed their address to the sender without saying they don't want messages and the message relates to their role, or within an existing business relationship; unsubscribe within 10 business days.

title: Event Data Lab Report #05: One in five registered attendees won't show up
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 29 April 2026. Check-in data from 1,070+ in-person events on PheedLoop's platform: median no-show about 20% (mean 29%); free about 28% vs paid about 17%; 10 to 49 expected attendees about 32%, levelling near 19% above 150. Vendor data.

title: 2026 Webinar Benchmarks
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 1 Sep 2026. 33,786 sessions held in 2025; average show-up rate 47.7%; 49.7% of registrations in the final 7 days and 15.3% on the day. Vendor data.

title: IAEE releases 2026 CEIR Index Report
publisher: International Association of Exhibitions and Events
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 4 May 2026. CEIR Total Index for US B2B exhibitions forecast to grow 2.1% in 2026; risks from trade policy, costs, geopolitics and travel expenses; index tracks net square feet, attendance, exhibitors and revenue.

title: CES 2026 draws nearly 150,000 attendees
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 20 April 2026, reporting CTA figures. 148,392 audited attendees, more than 4,100 exhibitors, about 1,200 startups in Eureka Park; third-party audited to UFI standards.

title: Adobe customer story (Adobe Summit 2020 moved online)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Vendor case study, undated; event spring 2020. About 23,000 attendees expected; in-person event cancelled a month before and relaunched online; registrations three times the goal; more than 700,000 online views; first LinkedIn Live 28,400 views in 24 hours.

title: Organizer pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. No fees for free events; per-ticket service fee and payment processing fee on paid tickets, passed to buyers by default; paid add-ons; plans offered in the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the UK and Ireland.

title: Zoom MCP servers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. Zoom publishes MCP servers with regional gateway URLs; OAuth, scoped permissions and admin controls; the page does not list a full tool set.

title: Sustainability Events Standards
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated (graphic 'as of October 2026'). Eight sector standards including venue, event organiser, exhibition services and food and beverage; criteria include climate, materials, supply chain, accessibility and social impact; levels from Foundations and Bronze to Platinum by share of criteria; third-party verification.

title: LinkedIn Conversions API
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated about three months before the check. Connects online and offline data, including in-person event leads, to LinkedIn campaigns; email hashed with SHA-256; data deleted after 180 days except aggregate reporting.

title: HubSpot MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated (footer 2026). Remote MCP server with OAuth; read and write for CRM records such as contacts, companies, deals and tasks; campaigns read-only.

title: Frequently Asked Questions (CCPA)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated. The CCPA's employee and business-to-business exemptions expired on 31 December 2022; coverage thresholds include $26.625 million gross revenue from 1 January 2025.
